proposals.before: Shi Yanbang, who held the south city, begged for relief and warned that missiles were almost gone.
proposals.after: Shi Yanshang, who held the south city, begged for relief and warned that missiles were almost gone.
proposals.reason: Chinese 氏延賞 is Shi Yanshang; Yanbang is a wrong romanization of 延賞.

proposals.before: South-city defender Shi Yanbang reported urgency and said arrows and stones were nearly spent.
proposals.after: South-city defender Shi Yanshang reported urgency and said arrows and stones were nearly spent.
proposals.reason: Chinese 氏延賞 should be romanized Shi Yanshang, not Shi Yanbang.

proposals.before: In the seventh month Liu Yan and Yin Hao of Liang struck Tong.
proposals.after: In the seventh month Liu Xun and Yin Hao of Liang struck Tong.
proposals.reason: Chinese 劉鄩 is Liu Xun; Yan is a wrong reading of 鄩.

proposals.before: Autumn, seventh month, Liang generals Liu Yan and Yin Hao raided Tong prefecture.
proposals.after: Autumn, seventh month, Liang generals Liu Xun and Yin Hao raided Tong prefecture.
proposals.reason: Chinese 劉鄩 is Liu Xun; Yan is a wrong reading of 鄩.

proposals.before: Liang sent Liu Yan and Yin Hao of Huazhou to invest Tong; Youqian cried for help, and Cunxu sent Li Cunshen as overall commander, Li Sizhao of Zhaoyi, and Wang Jianji of Dai to relieve him.
proposals.after: Liang sent Liu Xun and Yin Hao of Huazhou to invest Tong; Youqian cried for help, and Cunxu sent Li Cunshen as overall commander, Li Sizhao of Zhaoyi, and Wang Jianji of Dai to relieve him.
proposals.reason: Chinese 劉鄩 is Liu Xun; Yan is a wrong reading of 鄩.

proposals.before: The Liang ruler then sent Liu Yan and Huazhou military commissioner Yin Hao with troops to besiege Tong; Youqian reported the crisis, and the Emperor sent Chinese-and-tribal overall commander Li Cunshen, Zhaoyi commissioner Li Sizhao, and Dai prefecture commissioner Wang Jianji with armies to the relief.
proposals.after: The Liang ruler then sent Liu Xun and Huazhou military commissioner Yin Hao with troops to besiege Tong; Youqian reported the crisis, and the Emperor sent Chinese-and-tribal overall commander Li Cunshen, Zhaoyi commissioner Li Sizhao, and Dai prefecture commissioner Wang Jianji with armies to the relief.
proposals.reason: Chinese 劉鄩 is Liu Xun; Yan is a wrong reading of 鄩.

proposals.before: That night Liu Yan pulled the survivors into camp and never came out again.
proposals.after: That night Liu Xun pulled the survivors into camp and never came out again.

proposals.before: Within days Yan slipped away by night.
proposals.after: Within days Xun slipped away by night.

proposals.before: After several days Yan fled by night.
proposals.after: After several days Xun fled by night.

proposals.after: The royal army caught them at the Wei River; abandoned arms, gear, and baggage were beyond counting, and Liu Xun and Yin Hao alone on horseback escaped.
